narrativeReportMd:
# Communication R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Hard local breaking changes were found. The `Communication` resource itself retains the same identity, but R6 removes the protocol-instantiation fields, narrows `basedOn`, merges `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` into `reason: CodeableReference`, and replaces `payload.contentString` with `payload.contentCodeableConcept`.

## Scope
This assessment covers local `Communication` elements in the R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions. Inherited base-resource changes are explicitly out of scope; in particular, the `Resource.language` binding strengthening should be handled by the Resource/base-artifact analysis.

## Main migration themes
The largest migration theme is representation change rather than cardinality change. R4 instances can fail R6 validation because they contain element names that R6 no longer defines (`instantiatesCanonical`, `instantiatesUri`, `reasonCode`, `reasonReference`, `payload.contentString`). R6 also introduces richer representations (`Communication.reason` as `CodeableReference`, codified payload content, and Endpoint/Location/CareTeam participant references) that are not always losslessly representable back in R4.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `Communication.reason` and `Communication.payload.content[x]`, because they affect common code-generated properties and common instance shapes. `Communication.basedOn` is also a validation break for any R4 data that used the old any-Resource target flexibility.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for determining local migration policy: where removed instantiation links should go, how to pair or split R4 reason codes and reason references, and whether string payloads should become `CodeableConcept.text`, coded concepts, attachments, or references.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several R6 goals appear understandable: making request targets explicit, unifying code/reference reasons with `CodeableReference`, and allowing codified payload content. However, the removals could have been less disruptive if deprecated R4 aliases or transition extensions had been retained for one release.

## Follow-up analysis
Follow-up should cover the inherited `Resource.language` change, the `CodeableReference` datatype, and any official cross-version ConceptMaps or conversion maps for Communication.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 keeps `Communication` as the same concrete resource but introduces hard local instance breaks: removed instantiation elements, a narrowed `basedOn` target set, a `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` merge into `reason`, and replacement of string payload content with `CodeableConcept`. The main uncertainty is rationale and official migration guidance, not the computable deltas.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration work should focus on element-name and representation transforms rather than required-field backfill: no local cardinality minimums increased. Existing R4 `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` arrays need mapping into repeated `Communication.reason` CodeableReferences, and R4 `payload.contentString` needs a policy for `contentCodeableConcept.text` versus coded payloads. Systems that used `basedOn` for references outside the R6 request target list must choose a different relationship such as `about`, an extension, or a profile-specific mapping.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local structural, type, cardinality, modifier, and required-code comparisons because both primary StructureDefinitions and supporting package indexes were inspected directly. Confidence is lower for committee rationale, prevalence, and terminology-expansion details because official diffs, Jira/change notes, rendered narrative pages, and live terminology expansions were not supplied.

findings.title: Protocol instantiation elements were removed from Communication

oldState.summary: R4 allowed repeated canonical and URI links to protocols, guidelines, ordersets, or other definitions instantiated by the communication.

semanticText.short: Instantiates FHIR protocol or definition / Instantiates external protocol or definition
semanticText.definition: R4 represented the FHIR-defined and externally maintained protocol or definition adhered to by the Communication.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances could carry `instantiatesCanonical` and/or `instantiatesUri` to say that the communication followed a protocol, guideline, orderset, questionnaire, measure, or external definition.

newState.summary: R6 has no local `Communication.instantiatesCanonical` or `Communication.instantiatesUri` element.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 `Communication` local element list removes both instantiation fields and does not introduce an obvious same-name or direct replacement field.

facts.note: Both removed elements were summary elements in R4.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 snapshot and differential contain no elements with `instantiates` in the local `Communication` element set. No likely local replacement was found in the R6 Communication StructureDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and parser break for any R4 instance that contains either removed field: base R6 `Communication` does not define those element names. Code generated from R6 will also lack the old properties, so transforms or extensions are needed before loading old data into strict R6 models.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss of protocol or guideline linkage can affect auditability, quality reporting, and workflow provenance, even though it is not usually the clinical content of the message itself.

justification.inferredGoal: Likely simplification or alignment of Communication with the R6 event pattern by removing explicit protocol-instantiation links.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `instantiatesCanonical` and `instantiatesUri` as deprecated optional base elements while steering new R6 use away from them.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The likely goal, simplifying Communication or aligning it with the R6 event pattern, is reasonable. The supplied evidence does not show why achieving that goal required removing optional, non-modifier protocol-link elements from the base resource. Because those fields could have remained valid but deprecated, the break appears probably avoidable rather than clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design would keep `Communication.instantiatesCanonical` and `Communication.instantiatesUri` with the same optional cardinalities, mark them deprecated, and clarify that newer workflows should use the preferred R6 relationship. This is a base-design alternative, not a conversion extension. Its main cost is ongoing support for legacy protocol-link fields and the risk that deprecated representations never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances with modest model bloat, but keeps deprecated protocol-link representations that may persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `instantiatesCanonical` as 0..* canonical with target profiles PlanDefinition, ActivityDefinition, Measure, OperationDefinition, and Questionnaire.

evidence.locator: snapshot.element ids for local Communication elements
evidence.detail: R6 local `Communication` elements do not include `instantiatesCanonical` or `instantiatesUri`.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative only; no official cross-version extension for these removed elements was found in the supplied inputs.

findings.narrativeMd: `Communication.instantiatesCanonical` and `Communication.instantiatesUri` are local R4 fields that disappear from the R6 resource. Any historical Communication that used these fields to preserve the protocol or guideline followed by a message will fail strict R6 validation unless the data is transformed or carried in an extension.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance with either field becomes R6-invalid because the element names are unknown in the R6 StructureDefinition. The break is not inherited from a base artifact and does not depend on terminology expansion. R6-to-R4 is not the primary issue because R6 has no corresponding base element to send back.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory use of both R4 fields. If the canonical or URI is operationally important, define a local extension, map to a profile-specific relationship, or preserve the link outside the Communication resource. Regression tests should include Communications with only canonical links, only URI links, and both fields present.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the fields were optional and non-modifier, a backward-compatible design could have retained them while marking them deprecated. Removing them from the base resource gives a cleaner model but shifts the burden to cross-version extensions or out-of-band migration policy.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should confirm whether another R6 artifact or official conversion map provides a preferred home for these protocol links.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed `Communication.instantiatesCanonical` and `Communication.instantiatesUri` as optional summary elements for linking the communication to a protocol, guideline, order set, operation, questionnaire, or external definition. R6 removes both local elements without an equivalent replacement on `Communication`. An R4 communication that records that a notification followed a specific protocol can no longer validate as base R6 without moving that information elsewhere or using an extension. Because the fields were optional, non-modifier provenance links, retaining them as deprecated elements would likely have preserved old instances at relatively low base-model cost.
keyEvidence: R4 `Communication.instantiatesCanonical` is 0..* canonical targeting PlanDefinition, ActivityDefinition, Measure, OperationDefinition, and Questionnaire.
R4 `Communication.instantiatesUri` is 0..* uri for externally maintained protocols or definitions.
R6 Communication snapshot has no `instantiatesCanonical` or `instantiatesUri` local element.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Communication is FMM 2/trial-use, so maturity does not create a normative stability presumption; however FMM 2 is neutral rather than very-low, and the break affects optional but meaningful workflow/provenance fields.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: R4 JSON containing either removed property is not a valid R6 Communication shape, and R6 generated models will not expose the old fields.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A plausible less-breaking R6 base design was to keep both optional fields with deprecation guidance while steering new implementations to any preferred R6 pattern. The tradeoff is ongoing support for legacy protocol-link elements, but that seems modest compared with silently invalidating existing instances.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium hard-break assessment and the reported Yes less-breaking alternative; the fresh review puts the finding in Revisit because the removal looks avoidable.

findings.title: Communication.basedOn reference targets were narrowed from any Resource to named request resources

oldState.summary: R4 allowed `Communication.basedOn` to reference any Resource, with narrative guidance that it should be some sort of request.

semanticText.definition: An order, proposal or plan fulfilled in whole or in part by this Communication.
semanticText.comment: This must point to some sort of a 'Request' resource, such as CarePlan, CommunicationRequest, ServiceRequest, MedicationRequest, etc.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 model was structurally broad: a validator seeing `Reference(Resource)` could accept arbitrary resource types, even though the comment advised request-like resources.

newState.summary: R6 restricts `basedOn` to CarePlan, CommunicationRequest, DeviceRequest, MedicationRequest, NutritionOrder, ServiceRequest, Task, or VisionPrescription.

semanticText.definition: An order, proposal or plan fulfilled in whole or in part by this Communication.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 turns the R4 narrative expectation into a computable target-profile list.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged, but the `Reference.targetProfile` list changed from the generic Resource profile to a finite request-resource list.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance whose `basedOn.reference` points to a resource outside the R6 list can become invalid under R6 target-profile validation. The practical risk depends on whether validators can infer or resolve the referenced target type, but generated profiles and strict validators will treat the allowed set as narrower.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: `basedOn` establishes fulfillment of an order, proposal, or plan; incorrect migration can affect workflow traceability.

justification.inferredGoal: Make the request-like semantics of `basedOn` computable instead of relying on an R4 comment.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Reference(Resource)` and express request-like use with a base warning or best-practice invariant instead of a narrowed target-profile list.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: R4 already described `basedOn` as an order, proposal, or plan and said it must point to some sort of request resource. R6 makes that semantic expectation computable by enumerating request-like targets. A less-breaking design exists, but it would materially weaken the R6 goal, so the narrowing is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The partial alternative is to leave the base type as `Reference(Resource)` and add a warning, best-practice invariant, or profile guidance encouraging request resources. That preserves old references to non-request resources, but it leaves target validation ambiguous and gives generated R6 models no finite target set. An error-level invariant would itself become breaking, so the truly less-breaking version would only partially meet the R6 goal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve broad R4 data, but would not give validators, codegen, or interoperability rules the same computable request-resource target set.

evidence.detail: R4 target profile is the generic Resource profile.
R6 target profiles are a finite list of request-related resources.
evidence.quote: CarePlan | CommunicationRequest | DeviceRequest | MedicationRequest | NutritionOrder | ServiceRequest | Task | VisionPrescription

examples.examplesMd: The example shows the structural target-profile issue. Whether a particular validator flags it can depend on whether it resolves `Encounter/enc1` or infers the type from the literal reference.

findings.narrativeMd: `Communication.basedOn` kept its name and cardinality but lost the old any-Resource target flexibility. R4 data that used `basedOn` for non-request relationships can no longer rely on the base target profile in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation can fail for references outside the eight allowed R6 target profiles. R6-to-R4 representability is low risk because every R6 allowed target is still a Resource in R4. Runtime risk is mainly in code-generated validators, profile validators, and relationship-handling logic that assumed broad targets.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify existing `basedOn` targets. References to the R6 allowed request resources can migrate directly. Other references should be reviewed and remapped to a more appropriate relationship such as `about`, a local extension, or a profile-specific element. Test with both resolvable references and literal references whose type can be inferred from the reference string.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The narrowing is semantically defensible because R4 already described `basedOn` as a request relationship. It was not strictly necessary to change the base target profile; an invariant or profile could have preserved old structural compatibility while encouraging request-only use.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm whether local historical data used `basedOn` for non-request context links, because those are the instances affected by this change.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 made `Communication.basedOn` a `Reference(Resource)`, while its definition and comment described an order, proposal, plan, or other request-like source. R6 keeps the path and cardinality but narrows the target profiles to named request/workflow resources. A strict R6 validator can reject an R4 instance whose `basedOn` points to a non-listed resource, but that instance was already outside the element's stated request-oriented intent. Making the intended target set computable is a reasonable R6 goal.
keyEvidence: R4 `Communication.basedOn` is 0..* `Reference(Resource)` with comment that it must point to some sort of request resource.
R6 `Communication.basedOn` is 0..* Reference to CarePlan, CommunicationRequest, DeviceRequest, MedicationRequest, NutritionOrder, ServiceRequest, Task, or VisionPrescription.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use makes this a neutral maturity context: the target narrowing still matters, but the judgment turns mainly on the element's pre-existing semantics and the computable R6 goal.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: target-profile validation can reject R4 `basedOn` references outside the R6 finite request-resource list; generated APIs may also expose a narrower reference target set.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained `Reference(Resource)` and used prose, a warning, or profiles to encourage request-like targets. That would preserve more old data, but it would not meet the same base-level computability goal and would leave validators and code generators without a finite target set.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium impact and Partial alternative judgment: the alternative is real but materially weaker than the R6 design goal.

findings.title: R4 reasonCode and reasonReference were merged into Communication.reason CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 used two separate repeated elements: `reasonCode` as CodeableConcept and `reasonReference` as Reference to Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, or DocumentReference.

binding.description: Codes for describing reasons for the occurrence of a communication.

semanticText.short: Indication for message / Why was communication done?
semanticText.definition: The reason or justification for the communication; or another resource whose existence justifies this communication.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 separated coded reasons from resource reasons into two independent arrays. There was no built-in way to pair one code with one reference.

newState.summary: R6 has one repeated `reason` element of type CodeableReference(Resource), with the same example clinical-findings binding on the concept side.

binding.description: Codes for describing reasons for the occurrence of a communication.

semanticText.definition: The reason or justification for the communication.
semanticText.comment: Textual reasons can be captured using reason.concept.text.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 consolidates the two old arrays into `reason`, whose datatype can carry a `concept` and/or `reference` component. Its reference target is widened to any Resource.

facts.note: The reference branch is widened as part of the CodeableReference merge.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements share the same semantic label, summary flag, example binding, and purpose. R6 `Communication.reason` is the clear replacement for both R4 reason elements.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is both an instance-shape break and a codegen break. R4 JSON names `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` are not valid R6 element names, while R6 `reason` uses a datatype that did not exist in R4 and can reference any Resource. Bidirectional conversion needs active transformation and can be lossy or policy-dependent.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reasons can drive clinical interpretation, audit, and workflow rules; losing or mis-pairing reasons can change downstream behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Adopt the newer CodeableReference pattern to represent a reason as either a concept, a resource reference, or a combined concept/reference item.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `Communication.reason` as `CodeableReference` while retaining deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` for a transition period.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of using `CodeableReference` for a code-or-reference reason is reasonable and fixes a modeling split in R4. Keeping the old fields would be possible, but it would leave two parallel ways to state the same reason and would require rules for duplication, pairing, and precedence. Because those tradeoffs are material, the breaking merge is probably justified, not a clear `Yes` alternative case.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would add `reason` and keep `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as deprecated optional elements. That would let R4 instances validate unchanged while enabling new R6 instances to use `CodeableReference`. The cost is semantic duplication: a single Communication could carry reasons in both old and new forms, receivers would need reconciliation rules, and deprecated reason fields could accumulate indefinitely instead of converging on one representation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances but creates duplicate same-resource reason representations, ambiguous use rules, and legacy fields that may persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `reasonCode` as 0..* CodeableConcept with an example clinical-findings binding.
R4 defines `reasonReference` as 0..* Reference to Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, or DocumentReference.
R6 defines `reason` as 0..* CodeableReference targeting Resource with the same example clinical-findings binding.
R6 CodeableReference contains optional `concept` and `reference` child elements.

examples.examplesMd: The R4-to-R6 example maps each old array item to a separate CodeableReference. If an implementation had local semantics pairing codes with references by array position or other convention, manual review is needed.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 replaces two familiar R4 properties with a single `Communication.reason` property. This will surprise code generated from either version: R4 clients have `reasonCode` and `reasonReference`, while R6 clients expect an array of `CodeableReference` objects.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` are R6-invalid until transformed because those element names are absent. Valid R6 `reason.reference` values that point to resources other than Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, or DocumentReference cannot be represented in R4 `reasonReference` without an extension or a different relationship. The CodeableReference shape also changes JSON paths used by FHIRPath, search extraction, and business rules.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `reasonCode[]` to `reason[].concept` and `reasonReference[]` to `reason[].reference`. Do not assume lossless pairing between old codes and references unless local data conventions explicitly define that pairing. For R6-to-R4, split concepts and references back to the old arrays only when the reference target is one of the R4-allowed types; otherwise use an extension, `about`, or manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The unified CodeableReference model is likely justified, but the immediate removal of the R4 fields was avoidable. A deprecation period would have preserved instance compatibility while giving implementers time to move queries, validation rules, and generated model properties to `reason.concept` and `reason.reference`.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review local data to see whether reason codes and reason references were intended to be independent or paired. The base R4 model did not define pairing semantics.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 represented reasons with two separate repeated properties: `reasonCode` for coded/text reasons and `reasonReference` for references to a limited set of resources. R6 replaces both with repeated `reason` `CodeableReference(Resource)`. This is a real wire-format and generated-model break, and reverse conversion can lose information when an R6 reason uses a reference outside the old target list or combines concept and reference in one CodeableReference. Still, the R6 shape directly addresses the code-or-reference modeling split and uses a standard datatype for that purpose.
keyEvidence: R4 `Communication.reasonCode` is 0..* CodeableConcept with example clinical-findings binding.
R4 `Communication.reasonReference` is 0..* Reference to Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, or DocumentReference.
R6 `Communication.reason` is 0..* CodeableReference targeting Resource with the same example clinical-findings binding.
R6 CodeableReference has optional `concept` and `reference` children.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use softens the stability burden compared with mature or normative content, but this remains important because the path carries justification for the communication and affects generated models.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen and R6-to-R4 loss: old `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` names are invalid in R6, and some R6 CodeableReference uses cannot be represented cleanly in base R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have added `reason` while keeping deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference`. That would preserve R4 instances but create parallel representations for the same reason, requiring reconciliation and precedence rules when old and new fields coexist.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high impact and Partial alternative judgment: the migration burden is real, but the less-breaking alternative has substantial duplicate-representation costs.

findings.title: Communication.payload.content[x] removed string content and added CodeableConcept content

oldState.summary: R4 payload content was a required 1..1 choice among string, Attachment, or Reference(Resource).

semanticText.definition: A communicated content (or for multi-part communications, one portion of the communication).

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed simple text payloads using the primitive JSON property `contentString`.

newState.summary: R6 payload content remains 1..1 but the choices are Attachment, Reference(Resource), or CodeableConcept.

semanticText.definition: A communicated content (or for multi-part communications, one portion of the communication).
semanticText.comment: If the content is not codified, contentCodeableConcept.text can be used. When using contentCodeableConcept, the CodeableConcept is what is being communicated and is not a categorization of the content.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes the primitive string branch and uses `contentCodeableConcept` for textual or codified payload content.

facts.note: R4 JSON `contentString` is not an R6 choice.
R6 JSON `contentCodeableConcept` is not an R4 choice.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged, and the old/new type arrays show a direct choice-domain replacement: `string` was removed and `CodeableConcept` was added.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 payload that used `contentString` becomes invalid in R6. Generated classes, serializers, database columns, and FHIRPath expressions that reference `payload.contentString` must change. Conversely, R6 coded payload content cannot be represented in R4 without a lossy text conversion, an Attachment, a referenced resource, or an extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Payload is the communicated content. A lossy conversion can alter message meaning, especially when R6 uses codings rather than free text.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow payload content to be codified while still permitting textual content through CodeableConcept.text.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `CodeableConcept` as a new payload content choice while retaining `string` as a deprecated choice.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing codified payload content is a reasonable R6 goal, and `CodeableConcept.text` can carry uncoded text. The breaking part is removing the primitive `string` choice. Since FHIR choice elements can support multiple alternatives, adding `CodeableConcept` without removing `string` would have met the goal with only moderate long-term tradeoff.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design would make the choice set `string | Attachment | Reference | CodeableConcept`, mark `string` deprecated, and direct new implementations to `contentCodeableConcept.text` for text and codings for coded payloads. Receivers would need to normalize both `contentString` and `contentCodeableConcept.text`, and the old string representation might persist, but the alternative preserves most R4-valid payloads while still enabling codified R6 content.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Creates two ways to carry free text and requires normalization, but preserves R4 `contentString` instances while meeting the codified-payload goal.

evidence.detail: R4 choice types are string, Attachment, and Reference(Resource).
R6 choice types are Attachment, Reference(Resource), and CodeableConcept.
R6 says non-codified content can use `contentCodeableConcept.text` and that CodeableConcept is the communicated content, not a category.

examples.examplesMd: The R4-to-R6 text migration to `contentCodeableConcept.text` is usually semantically close for pure text, but it changes the JSON element name and datatype.

findings.narrativeMd: `Communication.payload.content[x]` is a high-impact local choice change. The element still requires exactly one content choice inside each payload item, but one of the most implementation-friendly R4 choices, `string`, is no longer legal in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `contentString` is old-valid/new-invalid. R6 `contentCodeableConcept` is not R4-representable as a base element, and coded content may lose semantics if flattened into text. Strict serializers and generated models will need property-level changes from `contentString` to `contentCodeableConcept`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For text-only payloads, map `contentString` to `contentCodeableConcept.text` unless local policy chooses Attachment or a referenced resource. For coded R6 payloads, decide whether the coding can be safely downgraded to text for R4, or whether an extension/cross-version profile is required. Test payloads with simple text, coded concepts, attachments, and references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The added codified payload capability is useful, but removing `string` was avoidable. Keeping `string` alongside `CodeableConcept` would have preserved R4 data and let implementations gradually normalize text payloads.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because payload carries the actual communicated message part, automated migration should avoid collapsing coded content to text without clinical or business review.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 payload content could be a primitive string, Attachment, or Reference(Resource). R6 removes the string choice and adds CodeableConcept, with prose saying uncoded text can be carried in `contentCodeableConcept.text`. Since `payload.content[x]` is required within each payload item, any R4 payload using `contentString` needs a wire-format transform before it can validate as R6. The R6 goal of allowing coded payloads is reasonable, but removing the existing string choice looks like avoidable churn on the core communicated content.
keyEvidence: R4 `Communication.payload.content[x]` is 1..1 with types string, Attachment, and Reference(Resource).
R6 `Communication.payload.content[x]` is 1..1 with types Attachment, Reference(Resource), and CodeableConcept.
R6 comment says non-codified content can use `contentCodeableConcept.text` and that CodeableConcept is the content, not a category.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral, but payload content is central to the resource's practical use; the maturity level does not by itself justify changing a common wire representation when an additive option appears available.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen and R6-to-R4 loss: `contentString` instances are invalid in R6, generated serializers change, and coded R6 payloads cannot round-trip to R4 without policy or loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have widened the choice to `string | Attachment | Reference | CodeableConcept`, marked string as deprecated, and recommended `contentCodeableConcept.text` for new text payloads. That creates two ways to carry free text and requires normalization, but it preserves R4 instances while still enabling coded payloads.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high impact and Yes less-breaking alternative judgment; the fresh review also sees this as a Revisit case because the additive design seems straightforward.

findings.title: Sender and recipient reference targets were widened for R6 participants

oldState.summary: R4 sender and recipient allowed people, organizations, devices, healthcare services, and some care actors; recipient also allowed Group and CareTeam.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not allow Endpoint as a sender or recipient, did not allow Location as a recipient, and did not allow CareTeam as a sender.

newState.summary: R6 adds Endpoint to both sender and recipient, Location to recipient, and CareTeam to sender.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 participant model better supports endpoint-based routing and location/care-team actors, but those new targets are outside R4 participant target sets.

facts.note: No R4 sender/recipient target was removed.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element ids and paths are unchanged; the R6 targetProfile lists are supersets of the R4 lists for these two elements.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 break because the allowed target sets widened. It is material for R6-to-R4 conversion and for R4 clients consuming R6 data: new Endpoint, Location, or sender CareTeam references cannot be represented as valid base R4 `sender`/`recipient` targets.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Participant target differences can affect routing or audit interpretation, especially when Endpoint is used as the actual communication endpoint.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent modern communication participants such as technical endpoints, locations, and care teams more directly.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: sender and recipient target-profile widening preserves R4-valid instances; the issue is only R6-to-R4/down-conversion.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding Endpoint, Location, and CareTeam targets is a reasonable expressiveness improvement and does not reject any R4 sender or recipient target that was previously valid. The representability problem runs from R6 back to R4, so this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because R6 only adds participant target profiles and removes none, all R4-valid sender and recipient references remain compatible with respect to these target lists. R6 could avoid the down-conversion issue only by not adding the new target types, which would reduce expressiveness rather than provide a backward-compatible alternative to a break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility; R4 backports or extensions are migration mitigations, not base alternatives.

examples.examplesMd: The example is valid only with respect to the participant target-profile changes shown here; a complete instance may require referenced resources or profiles in a real validator.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 expands who or what can be the sender or recipient of a Communication. This is useful for R6 modeling, but it means R6 data can use participant references that R4 base validators and codegen did not allow.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid solely because of these additions. The risk runs the other way: an R6 instance with Endpoint, Location-as-recipient, or CareTeam-as-sender is not cleanly representable in R4 without moving the participant to an extension or another relationship.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R4-to-R6 migration can preserve existing sender/recipient values. R6-to-R4 conversion should detect new target types and either use a local extension, map to Organization/HealthcareService when clinically and operationally correct, or flag for manual review. Do not silently drop Endpoint references, because they may be the actionable routing address.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additions are backward compatible in the R4-to-R6 direction. Down-conversion cannot be made lossless using only R4 base elements because the R4 target sets are fixed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: For `sender` and `recipient`, R6 keeps the same element paths and expands the allowed target profiles. Existing R4 participant references remain within the R6 target sets. New R6 references to Endpoint, Location, or sender CareTeam may not down-convert to base R4, but that is a reverse-direction representability issue caused by an additive/widening change, not an R4-to-R6 compatibility break.
keyEvidence: R4 recipient targets include Device, Organization, Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, RelatedPerson, Group, CareTeam, and HealthcareService.
R6 recipient targets retain the R4 set and add Location and Endpoint.
R4 sender targets include Device, Organization, Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, RelatedPerson, and HealthcareService.
R6 sender targets retain the R4 set and add Endpoint and CareTeam.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use does not raise a stability concern because the change widens the allowed R6 target set and preserves R4-valid instances.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss only: some new R6 participant targets cannot be represented in base R4, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break for these paths.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for forward compatibility. Avoiding the new target types would reduce R6 expressiveness rather than preserve R4 instances, and R4 backports or extensions are migration mitigations rather than base-design alternatives.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with treating the medium reverse-conversion concern as a meaningful R4-to-R6 problem; agree that no backward-compatible alternative is applicable.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, baseDefinition, and abstract flag are unchanged. Maturity/status changes are recorded as non-breaking notable changes.
No local element that exists in both R4 and R6 changed min or max cardinality. The hard breaks are element removals/replacements, choice-domain changes, and reference-target changes.

`Communication.status` remains a local modifier element with cardinality 1..1, and no other local Communication element gained or lost modifier status. Inherited modifier-extension behavior is out of scope.

No summary-flag-only change was found on unchanged local elements. Removed R4 summary elements (`instantiatesCanonical`, `instantiatesUri`, `reasonCode`, `reasonReference`) and the new summary `reason` are covered in findings as element/model changes rather than flag-only changes.

The required `status` and `priority` bindings point to R6-versioned value sets, but the local CodeSystem code lists are unchanged (`event-status`: preparation, in-progress, not-done, on-hold, stopped, completed, entered-in-error, unknown; `request-priority`: routine, urgent, asap, stat). Example binding compose definitions for communication category/topic/not-done reason and clinical findings were unchanged, but live expansions were not performed.

No local Communication-specific invariant was added, removed, or strengthened. Apparent changes to `ele-1`, `dom-*`, and extension constraints are inherited/base-artifact topics and are excluded from findings.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value was found in either version for Communication elements.
No local slicing change was found for Communication. Slicing on inherited extension elements belongs to base/infrastructure artifacts.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraint changes were found.
